Markets are likely to read it as a slowdown in the rate of growth rather than a contraction, so there's limited near-term risk for AI-linked equities. Still, it adds to the debate over 2027 earnings expectations for the sector. For the Singapore dollar, firm near-term growth supports the MAS keeping its current settings in January, while the softer 2027 outlook limits the case for any further tightening. --- Singapore's message is that the AI boom isn't ending, it's just growing more slowly, and for an economy this exposed to it, that alone is enough to roughly halve growth next year.

title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6757 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

title: NinjaTrader Bid/Ask data change: does it affect your indicators and Tick Replay?
body: Well, I got this from NT. Once my heart rate subsided (What does this mean???) I investigated. In a nutshell, NinjaTrader is cutting a data series hardly anyone uses but that clogged its servers, and the bid/ask stamp that order flow traders depend on stays exactly where it is. Summary: NinjaTrader's historical data servers will no longer provide separate historical Bid and Ask data series The company says fewer than 1% of users load them, but recording them made up most of its historical server load Charts, indicators and strategies built on Last price are unaffected Tick Replay and order flow tools still work, because each historical trade keeps the bid and ask at the moment it happened Scripts that add a standalone Bid or Ask series via AddDataSeries will lose their historical backfill and need checking If a data source has no bid/ask on its trades, NinjaTrader substitutes values, so order flow readings on that data won't be accurate NinjaTrader is retiring the separate historical Bid and Ask data series from its historical data servers, but most traders, including those who rely on Tick Replay and order flow tools, should see no change. Charts, indicators and strategies built on Last price will work exactly as before. The one group that needs to check its setup is anyone whose charts or code load a standalone Bid or Ask series to build history. What exactly is NinjaTrader changing?

title: Goldman says AI's next test is proving the economics, not the technology
body: Goldman's focus on financing favours companies with strong balance sheets and reliable access to capital, which could widen the valuation gap between cash-rich hyperscalers and highly leveraged AI builders. Its view that agentic AI could push computing demand beyond user growth supports the chip, memory and power supply chain, consistent with its earlier note on AI spending broadening beyond Nvidia. Its expectation that permit and power constraints will shift where capacity is built, not reduce it, points to rising demand for sites with available energy, a theme relevant to utilities and energy markets. For newly listed AI names, the note's emphasis on execution suggests trading will stay sensitive to revenue updates. --- The big news Monday: Jensen Huang is back in charge. Nvidia moves higher. --- Goldman's verdict: AI demand looks real, but the industry now has to prove it can pay for the computing that demand requires, and not every player will.

title: Tokyo gets its first look at the Nvidia whiplash as Asia trades the Huang rebound
body: Asian chip stocks get their first full chance today to respond to Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive, and the setup differs sharply from market to market. Tokyo is the clearest case. Japanese markets were shut on Monday for a public holiday, so today's session is the first since Friday's AI-led sell-off on Wall Street and Monday's sharp rebound, when the Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.5%. Chip equipment and testing names with close ties to the AI supply chain, such as Advantest and Tokyo Electron, will be the ones to watch. Seoul has the most ground to recover. The Kospi fell 3.3% to around 4,709 on Monday, with Samsung Electronics down about 3% and SK Hynix down 2.5%, as the region traded Friday's US losses before the Huang news broke. Both memory makers are heavily exposed to AI demand, and US memory chip peer Micron jumped sharply overnight. Goldman Sachs also said in a recent note that demand is outstripping supply in memory, one of the areas where AI investment is increasingly flowing beyond Nvidia. Taiwan may have less catching up to do. The Taiex rose 2.2% on Monday and TSMC gained 1.5%, so some of the AI optimism was already priced in before the announcement. TSMC's role in advanced packaging, another bottleneck Goldman highlighted, still leaves it well placed if the rebound holds. Japan's flash PMIs at 0030 GMT (1930 US Eastern) add a macro test early in the session.

title: Goldman sees up to $15 trillion for AI infrastructure as spending spreads beyond Nvidia
body: Goldman's framing favours the bottleneck parts of the AI supply chain, particularly memory makers, advanced packaging specialists and power infrastructure, over a single-stock bet on Nvidia. The view that neocloud lending now depends on milestones should ease some credit concerns around the sector, although it also implies slower, more conditional build-outs. The power angle ties AI spending to energy and utilities demand, a theme that is likely to keep electricity infrastructure in focus as data centre construction grows. --- Goldman's message is that the AI build-out is bigger than any one company: even if Nvidia's share shrinks, the trillions keep flowing, just into more hands.
